findings.issue: New supporting-proof skip validates source/runtime/review hashes but does not validate the schema2 ownership contract or require the exact canonical record successful preflight. It can skip an autonomous note with Type, claim_id or primary runner if a malformed record lists it as a supporting proof. It also does not itself check direct owner citation and declared runner input. These are required by UNIT_RECEIPT, and immutable hashes establish identity rather than validity.
findings.concrete_scenario: A unit lists docs/OWNER.md and docs/CHILD.md as sources, with CHILD runtime hash matching its source hash and an exact bound reviewer report. Its schema2 supporting_proofs lists CHILD owned by OWNER, but CHILD also declares Type: bounded_theorem and a primary runner. Every added assertion passes and CHILD bypasses the normal Type/primary/helper checks. A proper exact-record preflight rejects this duplicate classification. Later pipeline may reject counts, but the new cheap gate does not establish its claimed classification before expensive work.
findings.narrow_fix: Require a successful actual review_receipt preflight whose input_record SHA binds this exact record and whose source tree/base matches the candidate, or perform equivalent actual-API identity, owner-link and declared-input validation before the skip. If the coordinator already enforces and hashes that exact receipt outside these scripts, bind/name that prerequisite explicitly and this concern is discharged.
